rationale: The supplied proof of rectifiable_c1_chart_pieces combines two independent, reusable obligations; a short assembly then finishes it. (1) lipschitz_open_charts covers parent steps 1-4 after Lemma 1.2 has been applied. Take a C¹-submanifold cover M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃ S_i inside an open U where f is locally Lipschitz. Choose charts, apply Lindelöf in ℝᴺ, then Lindelöf in ℝⁿ (through a countable basis), use the mean-value Lipschitz bound on closed balls and compose. This gives countably many open pieces (D_α, ψ_α) with ψ_α C¹, injective and Lipschitz with injective derivative, f∘ψ_α Lipschitz, and M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃ ψ_α(D_α). It is a purely topological/differential covering lemma, usable by every branch that consumes the Lemma 1.2 cover. (2) first_order_agreement covers parent steps 5-7 for one piece. A map Lipschitz on an open D ⊆ ℝⁿ agrees in value and Fréchet derivative with C¹ maps G_i on Borel sets E_i ⊆ D, and Lⁿ(D \ ⋃E_i) = 0. The proof uses Lipschitz extension, the C¹ approximation hypothesis for (n, m) with ε = (i+1)⁻¹, Borel agreement sets and Rademacher. This is the standard corollary of C¹ approximation (Simon Ch. 2 Thm 1.5; cf. Federer 3.1.16, Evans–Gariepy Thm 6.11). The parent keeps steps 1, 8 and 9. It obtains (N₀, S) from (hSC n ℓ M).1 hM and applies child (1) with N := n+ℓ. For each α it applies child (2) with hC1 n m to h := f ∘ ψ_α on D_α (choose). It re-indexes (α, i) by Nat.unpair/Nat.pair. Finally M \ ⋃_j ψ_j(E_j) ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_α ψ_α(D_α \ ⋃_i E_{α,i}), and these sets are Hⁿ-null by SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume. Verification: everything was run with lake env lean after import GMT.Ch03.Submission, under the replayed Contract scope used by gmt-compare.py. (a) Both child types pass lean_contract.validate_lean_statement and elaborate with autoImplicit false. (b) A theorem with the two child types as hypotheses proves the exact frozen parent type from dag.json, with no sorry. (c) Complete Lean proofs of both children also compile. The git-ignored GMT/Scratch/ChartPiecesSplitFull.lean (199 lines) declares Submission.submanifold_cover_lipschitz_open_charts, Submission.lipschitzOn_open_c1_first_order_agreement and Submission.rectifiable_c1_chart_pieces (the frozen parent type, proved from the two) plus HumanizeNodeComparator.target wrappers. All depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The children are independent (no sibling dependencies). They do not mention SubmanifoldCoverCharacterization or CountablyRectifiable, which only the parent consumes. Their names collide with nothing in dag.json, DAG.md, issue-workers.json, Mathlib or SimonGMT. subproblems.title: Countably many Lipschitz open chart pieces covering a C¹-submanifold cover inside U (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 / Remark 1.3 local representations)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N m : ℕ) (M U N₀ : Set (Rn N)) (S : ℕ → Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn m), IsOpen U → M ⊆ U → LocallyLipschitzOn U f → (∀ i, IsC1Submanifold n (S i)) → M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃ i, S i → ∃ (D : ℕ → Set (Rn n)) (ψ : ℕ → Rn n → Rn N), (∀ α, IsOpen (D α)) ∧ (∀ α, ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (ψ α) (D α)) ∧ (∀ α, InjOn (ψ α) (D α)) ∧ (∀ α, ∃ K, LipschitzOnWith K (ψ α) (D α)) ∧ (∀ α, ∀ u ∈ D α, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ (ψ α) u)) ∧ (∀ α, ∃ K, LipschitzOnWith K (f ∘ ψ α) (D α)) ∧ M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃ α, ψ α '' D α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 1-4. These rest on Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 and Remark 1.3 (chapter-03.txt lines 25-73): an embedded submanifold has local C¹ representations ψ : V → ℝ^{n+ℓ}, and such maps 'are automatically Lipschitz in each closed ball ⊂ V'. They also follow the procedure of the area formula (lines 376-381). Specialisations, stated explicitly:
- The submanifold cover that the parent obtains from Lemma 1.2 in its step 1 is a hypothesis here.
- The properness clause of IsC1Submanifold is not used.
- The parent's second Lindelöf step ('countably many of the balls B_{r_u}(u) cover V′') is carried out through a countable basis of ℝⁿ. The pieces D_α are therefore basis sets contained in such balls.
Notation: B(u, r) is the open ball, closedBall(u, r) the closed ball, and Dφ(u) = fderiv ℝ φ u.
Call a pair (D, φ), with D ⊆ ℝⁿ and φ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ, good if:
(G1) D is open;
(G2) φ is C¹ on D;
(G3) φ is injective on D;
(G4) φ is Lipschitz on D with some constant in ℝ≥0;
(G5) Dφ(u) is injective for every u ∈ D;
(G6) f∘φ is Lipschitz on D with some constant.
(G1)-(G6) are exactly the first six conjuncts of the conclusion for a pair (D_α, ψ_α).
1. (Charts.) For every i ∈ ℕ and y ∈ S_i, IsC1Submanifold n (S_i) provides an open V_{i,y} ⊆ ℝⁿ, an open W_{i,y} ⊆ ℝᴺ with y ∈ W_{i,y}, and ψ_{i,y} : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ. The map ψ_{i,y} is C¹ on V_{i,y}, injective on V_{i,y}, satisfies ψ_{i,y}(V_{i,y}) = W_{i,y} ∩ S_i, and Dψ_{i,y}(u) is injective for every u ∈ V_{i,y}. Fix such a choice for all (i, y).
2. (Countably many charts per S_i; Lindelöf in ℝᴺ.) Fix i. ℝᴺ is second countable and the sets W_{i,y}, y ∈ S_i, are open. So there is a countable T_i ⊆ S_i with ⋃_{y∈T_i} W_{i,y} = ⋃_{y∈S_i} W_{i,y} (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_biUnion_countable). Since y ∈ W_{i,y} for every y ∈ S_i, S_i ⊆ ⋃_{y∈T_i} W_{i,y}.
3. (The enumeration.) Let 𝔅 be a countable basis of the topology of ℝⁿ (TopologicalSpace.exists_countable_basis); its members are open sets. Let 𝒬 consist of the pair (∅, 0) together with all pairs (B, ψ_{i,y}) with i ∈ ℕ, y ∈ T_i and B ∈ 𝔅. Let 𝒫 := {p ∈ 𝒬 : p is good}.
- 𝒬 is countable: it is one point plus a countable union over i ∈ ℕ of countable unions over y ∈ T_i of the countable sets {(B, ψ_{i,y}) : B ∈ 𝔅}. Hence 𝒫 is countable.
- The pair (∅, 0) is good. ∅ is open, and (G2)-(G6) hold vacuously on ∅: every map is C¹, injective and K-Lipschitz on ∅ for any K, e.g. K = 0, and there is no u ∈ ∅.
- So 𝒫 is countable and nonempty, and there is a surjection ℕ → 𝒫, α ↦ (D_α, ψ_α) (Set.Countable.exists_eq_range).
Each (D_α, ψ_α) ∈ 𝒫 is good, which proves the first six conjuncts.
4. (Coverage: a point of M off N₀ lies in a chart.) Let x ∈ M; we show x ∈ N₀ ∪ ⋃_α ψ_α(D_α). If x ∈ N₀ this is clear. Otherwise M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_i S_i gives i with x ∈ S_i, and step 2 gives y ∈ T_i ⊆ S_i with x ∈ W_{i,y}. Write V := V_{i,y} and ψ := ψ_{i,y}. Then x ∈ W_{i,y} ∩ S_i = ψ(V), so x = ψ(u) for some u ∈ V. Moreover x ∈ U because M ⊆ U.
5. (A good radius at u.) Since f is locally Lipschitz on U and x ∈ U, there are K ∈ ℝ≥0 and t ∈ 𝓝[U] x with f K-Lipschitz on t. As U is open, 𝓝[U] x = 𝓝 x, so B(x, s) ⊆ t for some s > 0, and f is K-Lipschitz on B(x, s). ψ is continuous on V (C¹ implies continuous) and V is an open neighbourhood of u, so ψ is continuous at u. Since x = ψ(u), V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B(x, s)) is then a neighbourhood of u. Choose δ > 0 with B(u, δ) ⊆ V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B(x, s)) and put r := δ/2 > 0. Then closedBall(u, r) ⊆ B(u, δ) ⊆ V and ψ(closedBall(u, r)) ⊆ B(x, s).
6. (Lipschitz bound for ψ.) closedBall(u, r) is convex and compact (ℝⁿ is proper) and contained in V, on which ψ is C¹. A C¹ map on a compact convex set is Lipschitz there: its derivative is continuous, hence bounded on the compact set, and the mean value inequality applies (Mathlib ContDiffOn.exists_lipschitzOnWith with smoothness 1 ≠ 0). So ψ is L-Lipschitz on closedBall(u, r) for some L ∈ ℝ≥0.
7. (A good basis set at u.) B(u, r) is open and contains u, so there is B ∈ 𝔅 with u ∈ B ⊆ B(u, r) ⊆ closedBall(u, r) ⊆ V. The pair (B, ψ) is good:
(G1) B is open, being a basis set.
(G2), (G3) ψ is C¹ and injective on V ⊇ B.
(G4) ψ is L-Lipschitz on B ⊆ closedBall(u, r).
(G5) For v ∈ B ⊆ V, Dψ(v) is injective by step 1; fderiv is the derivative at the point and does not depend on the set.
(G6) ψ maps B into ψ(closedBall(u, r)) ⊆ B(x, s), on which f is K-Lipschitz, and ψ is L-Lipschitz on B. So f∘ψ is (K·L)-Lipschitz on B (composition of Lipschitz maps, LipschitzOnWith.comp with MapsTo).
8. (Conclusion.) Since i ∈ ℕ, y ∈ T_i and B ∈ 𝔅, the pair (B, ψ_{i,y}) lies in 𝒬. It is good by step 7, so it belongs to 𝒫. By surjectivity there is α with (D_α, ψ_α) = (B, ψ_{i,y}). Then u ∈ D_α and x = ψ_α(u) ∈ ψ_α(D_α). Hence M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_α ψ_α(D_α), which is the last conjunct. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose IsC1Submanifold charts (V_{i,y}, W_{i,y}, ψ_{i,y}) for every i and y ∈ S_i; Lindelöf in ℝᴺ gives a countable T_i ⊆ S_i with S_i ⊆ ⋃_{y∈T_i} W_{i,y}.
Fix a countable basis 𝔅 of ℝⁿ. The good pairs among (∅, 0) and (B, ψ_{i,y}) (i ∈ ℕ, y ∈ T_i, B ∈ 𝔅) form a countable nonempty set. Enumerate it surjectively by ℕ; this gives the six chart properties.
Coverage: x ∈ M \ N₀ lies in W_{i,y} ∩ S_i = ψ_{i,y}(V_{i,y}) for some y ∈ T_i, so x = ψ_{i,y}(u) with u ∈ V_{i,y}, and x ∈ U.

Local Lipschitz continuity of f at x and continuity of ψ_{i,y} at u give r > 0 with closedBall(u, r) ⊆ V_{i,y} and ψ_{i,y}(closedBall(u, r)) inside a ball where f is Lipschitz. ψ_{i,y} is Lipschitz on that compact convex closed ball (C¹ ⇒ Lipschitz).
A basis set B with u ∈ B ⊆ B(u, r) makes (B, ψ_{i,y}) good (by restriction and composition), so it equals some (D_α, ψ_α) and x ∈ ψ_α(D_α).

subproblems.title: First-order agreement of a Lipschitz map on an open set with C¹ maps off an Lⁿ-null set (Simon Ch. 2, Thms 1.2, 1.4, 1.5)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n m : ℕ), (∀ (F : Rn n → Rn m) (K : ℝ≥0), LipschitzWith K F → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ g : Rn n → Rn m, ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ volume {x | F x ≠ g x ∨ fderiv ℝ F x ≠ fderiv ℝ g x} < ε) → ∀ (D : Set (Rn n)) (h : Rn n → Rn m), IsOpen D → (∃ K, LipschitzOnWith K h D) → ∃ (G : ℕ → Rn n → Rn m) (E : ℕ → Set (Rn n)), (∀ i, ContDiff ℝ 1 (G i)) ∧ (∀ i, MeasurableSet (E i)) ∧ (∀ i, E i ⊆ D) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ u ∈ E i, h u = G i u ∧ HasFDerivAt h (fderiv ℝ (G i) u) u) ∧ volume (D \ ⋃ i, E i) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 5-7. These follow Simon Ch. 3, the procedure of the area formula (chapter-03.txt lines 376-381), invoked for the co-area formula at lines 426-428. They use from Simon Ch. 2: the Lipschitz extension Theorem 1.2 (chapter-02.txt lines 33-52), applied coordinatewise; Rademacher's Theorem 1.4 (lines 62-70); and the C¹ Approximation Theorem 1.5 (lines 165-169), supplied here as the hypothesis (C1_{n,m}). Specialisations, stated explicitly: the parent applies this to h = f∘ψ_α on D_α, whereas here h and D are arbitrary; and ε_i = (i+1)⁻¹, i ∈ ℕ, replaces the parent's 1/i, i ≥ 1. Notation: Lⁿ = volume and DF(u) = fderiv ℝ F u. Fix K ∈ ℝ≥0 with h K-Lipschitz on D.
1. (Global Lipschitz extension.) ℝᵐ is a finite-dimensional real normed space. So there is h̃ : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ with h̃ = h on D that is K̃-Lipschitz on all of ℝⁿ, where K̃ := lipschitzExtensionConstant(ℝᵐ)·K ∈ ℝ≥0 (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_finite_dimension; this is Simon Ch. 2, Thm 1.2 applied to the coordinates).
2. (C¹ approximants.) For i ∈ ℕ let ε_i := (i+1)⁻¹ ∈ ℝ≥0∞; ε_i > 0 because i+1 ≠ ∞. Apply (C1_{n,m}) to F := h̃ (which is K̃-Lipschitz) and ε_i. This gives G_i : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ of class C¹ with Lⁿ(Bad_i) < ε_i, where Bad_i := {u : h̃(u) ≠ G_i(u) or Dh̃(u) ≠ DG_i(u)}. This proves the first conjunct.
3. (Definition of E_i.) Let Diff := {u ∈ ℝⁿ : h̃ is differentiable at u} and E_i := D ∩ Diff ∩ {u : h̃(u) = G_i(u)} ∩ {u : Dh̃(u) = DG_i(u)}. Then E_i ⊆ D, which is the third conjunct.
4. (E_i is Borel; second conjunct.) The four sets in the intersection are Borel:
- D is open, hence Borel.
- Diff is Borel (measurableSet_of_differentiableAt; ℝᵐ is complete).
- h̃ (Lipschitz) and G_i (C¹) are continuous, so {h̃ = G_i} is closed (isClosed_eq), hence Borel.
- u ↦ Dh̃(u) and u ↦ DG_i(u) are Borel measurable maps into ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝᵐ with its Borel σ-algebra (measurable_fderiv). This space is finite-dimensional, hence second countable and metrizable, so its diagonal is measurable and {Dh̃ = DG_i} is Borel (measurableSet_eq_fun).
So E_i is Borel.
5. (Agreement to first order; fourth conjunct.) Let u ∈ E_i. Since u ∈ D, h(u) = h̃(u), and h̃(u) = G_i(u); so h(u) = G_i(u). Since u ∈ Diff, h̃ has Fréchet derivative Dh̃(u) at u, and Dh̃(u) = DG_i(u). So h̃ has Fréchet derivative DG_i(u) at u. D is open and contains u, so it is a neighbourhood of u on which h = h̃. Hence h has the same Fréchet derivative DG_i(u) at u (HasFDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq), i.e. HasFDerivAt h (fderiv ℝ G_i u) u.
6. (The exceptional set.) We claim D \ ⋃_i E_i ⊆ (ℝⁿ \ Diff) ∪ ⋂_i Bad_i. Let u ∈ D with u ∉ E_i for all i. If u ∉ Diff, u lies in the first set. If u ∈ Diff, then for every i, since u ∈ D ∩ Diff and u ∉ E_i, either h̃(u) ≠ G_i(u) or Dh̃(u) ≠ DG_i(u), i.e. u ∈ Bad_i. Hence u ∈ ⋂_i Bad_i.
7. (Measure zero; fifth conjunct.) h̃ is Lipschitz on ℝⁿ and Lⁿ is an additive Haar measure on ℝⁿ, so Rademacher's theorem (Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt) gives Lⁿ(ℝⁿ \ Diff) = 0. For every i, Lⁿ(⋂_k Bad_k) ≤ Lⁿ(Bad_i) < (i+1)⁻¹. Since (i+1)⁻¹ → 0 in ℝ≥0∞ (ENNReal.tendsto_inv_nat_nhds_zero), Lⁿ(⋂_k Bad_k) = 0. By step 6, monotonicity and subadditivity of Lⁿ, Lⁿ(D \ ⋃_i E_i) ≤ Lⁿ(ℝⁿ \ Diff) + Lⁿ(⋂_k Bad_k) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Extend h|_D to a globally Lipschitz h̃ : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ with h̃ = h on D (LipschitzOnWith.extend_finite_dimension).
Apply (C1_{n,m}) to h̃ with ε_i = (i+1)⁻¹. This gives C¹ maps G_i with Lⁿ(Bad_i) < (i+1)⁻¹, where Bad_i = {h̃ ≠ G_i} ∪ {Dh̃ ≠ DG_i}.
E_i := D ∩ Diff(h̃) ∩ {h̃ = G_i} ∩ {Dh̃ = DG_i} ⊆ D is Borel (measurableSet_of_differentiableAt, isClosed_eq, measurable_fderiv with measurableSet_eq_fun).
On E_i, h = h̃ near u because D is open, so h(u) = G_i(u) and HasFDerivAt h (DG_i(u)) u.
D \ ⋃E_i ⊆ (ℝⁿ \ Diff(h̃)) ∪ ⋂_i Bad_i. This set is Lⁿ-null: the first part by Rademacher, and Lⁿ(⋂ Bad_i) ≤ (i+1)⁻¹ → 0.
